title: UK Settlement Doubles to 10 Years: What Students Need
excerpt: Under Earned Settlement the standard route to UK permanent residence doubles from 5 to 10 years. See who still qualifies in 5 and what it means for international students.

content.html:
🏠 UK Earned Settlement — At a Glance
Standard Route10 Years (Was 5)
Faster Route5 Years for Higher Earners and Some Public Service Workers
Benefits Claimed20-Year Wait
Illegal EntryUp to 30 Years
Criminal RecordSettlement Blocked
EnglishHigher Standard (About B2)

What the Government Announced

On 2 November 2026 the government set out its Earned Settlement model in Parliament. The headline change: the right to live in the UK permanently, known as indefinite leave to remain (ILR), will no longer be granted automatically after five years. It will have to be earned.

GroupWait for settlement
Standard route10 years, up from 5
Higher earners above about £50,000 a year5 years
Skilled public service workers5 years
Refugees arriving on safe and legal routes5 years
Care workers who meet the visa requirements5-year route retained
Migrants who claim benefits20 years
People who enter illegally, including by small boatUp to 30 years

Every route also has conditions. Migrants with a criminal record will be prevented from settling, and applicants must meet a higher English standard, described as A-level standard and reported as B2.

⚠️
Details are still comingThe detailed Immigration Rules and guidance had not been published when this was written. Figures such as the earnings threshold and which benefits count may change in the final rules.

What Is Confirmed and What Is Not

QuestionWhere things stand
Is the standard wait 10 years?Yes, announced as the new standard route
Who qualifies in 5 years?Higher earners, skilled public service workers and refugees on safe and legal routes; care workers keep a 5-year route if they meet the visa requirements
Will it apply to people already in the UK?The stated intention is that anyone not yet granted settlement will be covered; transition details are still being set
When does it start?No single start date confirmed in the sources we reviewed
Does time on a Student or Graduate visa count?Not addressed in the sources we reviewed. Historically it has not counted toward settlement
Are people who already hold ILR affected?No. Those who already hold ILR keep it

What It Means for International Students

Studying in the UK does not lead to settlement on its own. Time on a Student visa or the Graduate visa has not counted toward the settlement clock, so students normally switch into a work route first, such as a Skilled Worker visa, and the settlement wait runs from there.

  • The long-term plan is longer. If you switch into the standard route, plan on a 10-year wait for ILR instead of 5, unless a shorter route applies.
  • Earnings matter more. A salary above about £50,000 can shorten the wait to 5 years. Many early-career salaries sit below that.
  • Your record matters. A criminal record, including minor convictions, can block settlement, and claiming specified benefits can lengthen the wait to 20 years.
  • English matters. You will need a higher English standard, so keep your test results strong.
  • Graduate visa length is changing too. See our guide to the Graduate visa from January 2027.

What To Do Now

  1. Treat settlement as a long-term goal.Decide whether you want a 3 to 5 year UK career or permanent residence, and plan for both outcomes.
  2. Choose your university and course for jobs.Pick a course with a clear route to a skilled job, because that is where the settlement clock starts.
  3. Keep your record clean.Follow your visa conditions and avoid any criminal record.
  4. Keep your English strong.Keep an approved English test result that can be renewed if needed.
  5. Check the final rules.Rules will appear on GOV.UK. We will update this guide when they do.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is UK settlement now 10 years?
Under the Earned Settlement model, the standard route doubles from 5 to 10 years, with shorter routes for some groups such as higher earners.
Who can still settle in 5 years?
Higher earners above about £50,000, skilled public service workers and refugees on safe and legal routes. Care workers who meet the visa requirements keep a 5-year route.
Does my Student or Graduate visa count?
The sources we reviewed do not say. Historically these visas have not counted toward settlement.
What English level is needed?
The government describes an A-level standard, reported as B2. Check the final rules.
Do I lose ILR if I already have it?
No. People who already hold ILR keep it.
Does claiming benefits affect settlement?
Claiming specified benefits can extend the wait to 20 years. Which benefits count is still being confirmed.
